Cancer is a terrible thing. The disease has plagued my family for generations. It was rare for any of my ancestors to live past 50, and so when I learned of this truth I dedicated my life to finding a cure. My entire adult life I have spent in labs, searching for something I knew must be there.

I never truly believed I would manage to find a cure, and with each passing year my faith grew thinner as I neared my death sentence.

I took no partner, fathered no children; I had pledged my life to the cause. When I turned 46, the cancer was already in advanced stages, yet I had refused to seek outside treatment. I had pushed away all who might be hurt by my demise due to the indomitable cancer.

The lab I resided in could have been mistaken for a mad scientist's lair, and in a way it might have actually been one. All sorts of animals were spread around in cages, each suffering from a different kind of cancer. Not a single treatment I tried worked. In some cases, the cancer even spread faster than previously.

The lab itself was located underground, near a main water line. The noise was hard to bear, but as my funding was cut almost completely I had to endure.

The situation was dire for me. I was alone, afraid, and in terrible pain, yet that is not an excuse for what I did next. An idea sprang into my mind in desperation; since I had failed in defeating the cursed disease, perhaps I could use it for a solution.

A new fire burned in my heart. Hope returned from its grave, and I worked harder than I had all those years past. It took me a year, seven months, and three days to complete my plan. At this point, the cancer had spread everywhere within my body. I knew my days were few in this world. I had no time for proper testing, and so I injected myself with the serum and then activated the device.

It is hard to explain exactly what changes happened in me and to me, but the short explanation is that first the cancer had to be helped, making it spread throughout the body completely, changing all cells to cancer cells. Secondly, the device I had built reprogrammed the changed cells to function without having to die.

It took me a while to wake up. I had basically died and was reborn then. I can't say I am the same as I was before the procedure, but the fact that a lot of my body was already made up of cancer cells made the transition less traumatic than it could have been.

When I finally managed to gain consciousness again, I woke in a place vastly different than the one I had been before. It appeared that during my coma, a disaster had hit my lab and most of my equipment was broken. Due to the water line nearby, the place was flooded.

My new body had to be put to the test immediately. I pushed and worked, and after a most painful period of time, I managed to break free to the surface. I did not know how I looked, as the lab was completely dark after its destruction, but I knew I had to get some help.

I walked the streets for a while before spotting a figure from afar. I shouted to them, yet they did not answer. It was only when I came closer that I could see that this was no person at all. A horrid twisted body stood in front of me, eating a fresh corpse of another horrid creature. I ran.

It seemed to not follow me, busy with its feeding. I walked a while more before finding a reflective surface. The view that was before me was the same as I saw before. To my horror, the transformation I had endured had made me a monster, but it did not explain the other monster.

I screamed in pain, asking why everything was all wrong. I had only wanted to live. It was then fire relieved me from my pain, and I suffered no more.
